scope: Theorem 1.1 (Uniform trace reconstruction) of the manuscript “Uniform quasipolynomial-time trace reconstruction” (preprints/Uniform-quasipolynomial-time-trace-reconstruction-October-5-2026/uniform-trace-reconstruction.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 122 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 cca17cd8900b5eda), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 1-2. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There exist absolute constants C, c ≥ 1 and one randomized multitape Turing machine A with the following property. For every n ≥ 2, every rational p ∈ (0, 1], and every x ∈ {0, 1}n, given n, p in binary and access to independent ordinary deletion traces of x, the machine requests at most MC(n, p) =  exp CB(n, p)  1 traces, outputs an element of {0, 1}n, and returns x with probability at least 2/3. For every internal random-bit sequence and every well-formed trace stream of strings of length at most n, it halts within n + L + MC(n, p) c bit operations. This bound includes preprocessing, all parameter and finite-precision calculations, every received trace bit and delimiter, and the output. The only oracle operation is the external generation of the independent deletion traces.
